successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Mauretania Tingitana (capital Tingis) and Mauretania Caesariensis (capital Caesarea), divided along the Mulucha (Moulouya) after Aedemon's revolt

ledger.x: 225 BC: Baga, the first documented king of Mauretania.
203 BC: King Bokkar of Morocco becomes Masinissa's vassal.
Early 2nd century BC: the Moroccan coast joins Mauretania.
105 BC: Bocchus I betrays Jugurtha and takes western Numidia.
49 BC: the court divides between two brothers.
49-45 BC: Bocchus II takes Cirta with Sittius.
After Caesar's murder (44 BC): Arabio recovers his father's land.
38 BC: Bocchus II reunites the kingdom.
33 BC: Bocchus II leaves Mauretania to Octavian.
25 BC: the eight years of Roman administration end.
25 BC: Juba II rules Mauretania as a client of Rome.
AD 23: Juba II dies and Ptolemy rules alone.
AD 44: Mauretania becomes two Roman provinces.

wars.name: Jugurthine War
wars.outcome: Bocchus I stayed neutral, allied with Jugurtha around 108 (promised a third of his kingdom), lost with him to Marius at the Second Battle of Cirta (106), then betrayed him to Sulla in 105 and took the western part of Numidia by treaty.

wars.name: Roman civil war in Africa (Bocchus and Sittius in Numidia)
wars.outcome: Bocchus and Sittius invaded Numidia on Caesar's side and seized Cirta 'within a few days'; Caesar gave Bocchus part of Masinissa II's land, which Arabio recovered after Caesar's murder.

wars.name: Revolt of Aedemon
wars.outcome: Aedemon, Ptolemy's freedman, rebelled after the execution of AD 40; Sabalus succeeded him and surrendered in 44; Rome made Mauretania Tingitana and Caesariensis.

certainty.note: Frontiers of a nomadic and Mauri kingdom with the Atlantic, the Moulouya and later the Ampsaga as natural limits; none was surveyed.
